ai.bookClosed: The assistant finished, but that essay was closed — nothing was added. Run it again from the essay.
ai.busy: The assistant is still working on something else
ai.cited: Cited — the source is now accepted
ai.critiqueThisDesc: The assistant marks its 3–7 most important issues with ✦.
ai.d.critiqueEssay: The whole essay — {sections} sections, {paras} paragraphs, {words} words
ai.d.research: ⚑ “{note}” — it searches the web and reads the pages it finds
ai.err.badKey: The API key is missing or was rejected — check it in Assistant Settings
ai.err.badModel: That model wasn’t accepted — pick another in Assistant Settings
ai.err.busy: The assistant is still working on something else
ai.err.failed: The assistant couldn’t finish — try again in a moment (details were logged)
ai.err.login: Claude Code isn’t logged in — run “claude” in a terminal and log in, then try again
ai.err.loginCodex: Codex isn’t logged in — run “codex login” in a terminal, then try again
ai.err.noCredit: The API account has no credit left — add credit with the provider
ai.err.noWeb: This service has no web access — research needs Claude Code, Codex or the Anthropic API
ai.err.notInstalled: Claude Code wasn’t found — install it, or set its path in Assistant Settings
ai.err.rateLimited: The service is rate-limiting you (or your plan’s limit was reached) — wait a moment
ai.err.tooLong: The assistant took too many steps and stopped — try again, or narrow the request
ai.err.unreachable: The server didn’t answer — check the URL, or that it’s running
ai.inBackground: Still working — you can follow it (or stop it) in the bar below
ai.intro: The assistant researches, critiques and suggests — it never changes your text without you accepting it. It runs through your own Claude Code: no API key needed.
ai.intro2: The assistant researches, critiques and suggests — it never changes your text without you accepting it. Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan through their own apps, or an API key.
ai.keepWritingTitle: Close this window; the task keeps going in the bar below and tells you when it is done
ai.keyNone: not needed for a local server
ai.keyNote: Stored encrypted on this computer, never in your library, and only sent to this service.
ai.keyNoteSaved: Type “remove” and save to forget the saved key.
ai.keySaved: •••••• saved — paste a new one to replace it
ai.markGone: That spot isn’t in the text anymore
ai.modelsNone: No models listed — check the URL and key, or type the model name
ai.needNote: Write in the note what you need to find out, then research it
ai.noIssues: The assistant found nothing important to flag
ai.noKeychain: No system keychain is available, so Mutiny won’t store the key (it never keeps keys in plain text). Start a keychain (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC), or set {env} in your environment.
ai.noMarksInside: Leave citations and marks out of the selection
ai.noWebNote: Research is off with this kind of service.
ai.off: The assistant is off — turn it on in Assistant Settings
ai.path: Path to claude (leave blank to find it)
ai.provNote.anthropic: Pay-as-you-go with an Anthropic API key (console.anthropic.com). Research, critique, rewrite and chat.
ai.provNote.claude-code: Uses the Claude Code installed on this computer and its login. Research, critique, rewrite and chat.
ai.provNote.codex: Uses OpenAI’s Codex CLI with your ChatGPT login, locked down (no shell, read-only). Research, critique, rewrite and chat.
ai.provNote.compat: Any server that speaks the OpenAI API. No web access: critique, rewrite and chat only.
ai.researchDone.one: Found 1 source — review it under the note
ai.researchDone.other: Found {n} sources — review them under the note
ai.rewritten: Replaced — your original is in Later ({undo} to undo)
ai.selectFirst: Select the words you want to improve, then {key}
ai.selectMore: Select at least a few words
ai.state.loggedOut: Claude Code {v} found, but not logged in — run “claude” in a terminal and log in.
ai.state.loggedOutCli: {name} {v} found, but not logged in — run “{cmd}” in a terminal and log in.
ai.state.missing: Claude Code wasn’t found on this computer. Install it (claude.com/claude-code) or give its path below.
ai.state.missingCli: {name} wasn’t found on this computer — install it, or give its path under Advanced.
ai.tooShort: There isn’t enough text here to critique yet
ai.usageApi: Pay-as-you-go: each request is billed to your API account. Mutiny shows what each answer cost when the service reports it.
ai.usageNote: Each request uses your Claude plan, just like using Claude Code. Research reads the web; critique and rewrite only see the text you send.
ai.usagePlan: Each request uses your plan’s limits, just like using the app itself.
author.addPenDesc: A separate set of shelves under another name
author.removeDesc: These shelves and essays move to your other name. Nothing is deleted from disk.
bar.goalTitle: Today’s words — click for goals, sprints, and your progress chart
bar.wordsTitle: Click to switch between essay and section word count
bar.zoomTitle: Scroll to zoom, or pinch / Ctrl+Scroll anywhere on the page
chat.clearNote: The conversation is deleted. Answers you moved to Notes stay there.
chat.empty:
Ask anything about your essay — the argument, the structure, what’s missing. The assistant reads the draft as it is right now.

Select text first to ask about just that part.
chat.off: The assistant is off. Turn it on in Assistant Settings to chat about your essay.
chat.placeholder: Ask about your essay… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter for a new line)
cite.candidate: This source hasn’t been reviewed yet — accept it in Sources to number it
cite.needSection: Click into the text first, then {key} cites
cite.noSources: No sources yet — paste a link above to add one.
cite.oneParagraph: Select words within one paragraph to cite them
cite.pickPh: Search your sources, or paste a link, DOI or ISBN…
cite.removeWordsDesc: The words stay; only the citation goes.
collection.empty: This shelf has no essays on it yet
collection.noWords: No words found on this shelf yet
collection.titleHint: Shown at the top of the document
cover.rerollAbstract: A fresh abstract and a different title style.
cover.rerollImage: Re-sets the title in a different style over the same art.
cover.showAbstractDesc: The seeded cover every essay starts with.
cover.showImageDesc: The image you gave this essay.
dialog.trashDetail: The essay folder goes to your system trash, so you can recover it.
dialog.trashFailed: Mutiny couldn’t move that folder to the Trash.
dialog.trashFailedDetail: The essay is untouched. Its folder is highlighted so you can deal with it yourself.
email.body3: SHA-256 fingerprint of the essay text:
email.bodyGmail: The PDF snapshot is in the folder Mutiny just opened — drag it into this email before sending.
email.gmailDesc: Opens a pre-filled compose window in your browser. Mutiny shows you the PDF to drag into it.
email.gmailOpened: Gmail compose opened — drag in the PDF Mutiny revealed, then send
email.mailDesc: Fully automatic — the PDF is attached and addressed. Just hit send.
email.mailDone: Draft handed to Mail — hit send for your timestamp
email.methodQ: How should Mutiny email your drafts?
email.subject: Mutiny draft — {title} — {words} — {date}
email.unavailable: Mail unavailable — snapshot saved to your Exports folder instead
font.systemNote: Hover to preview on the page. A system font isn’t bundled with Mutiny: on another computer without it, the page falls back to Literata.
fr.aiIntro: Mutiny can research the facts you mark, critique your argument and suggest better wording — through your own Claude Code. It never changes your text unless you accept.
fr.aiLater: You can turn it on now and log in later.
fr.aiOffDesc: Write without it. Turn it on later from the Assistant menu.
fr.aiOnDesc: You can turn it off anytime in the Assistant menu.
fr.aiTitle: An assistant, if you want one
fr.intro: Mutiny is for writing essays. A few quick questions and it will never ask again.
fr.lookIntro: Pick a typeface. The sample shows exactly what you’ll get. (Changeable anytime in the Format menu.)
fr.name: Your name
fr.nameHint: (appears as the author on every essay — leave blank for “Anonymous”)
fr.pantserDesc: New essays open on a blank page.
fr.penHint: (optional — a pen name, if you publish under one)
fr.plotterDesc: New essays open on an outline: a thesis and a handful of sentences to build on.
fr.sample: The city we walk is not the city we drive. One is measured in minutes of traffic; the other, in the people we pass on the way…
fr.voiceDoneDesc: Start writing. My voice waits on your shelves.
fr.voiceHint: 3 to 5 texts (5,000–10,000 words) are enough for a first profile. You can add them any time.
fr.voiceImportDesc: .docx, .md or .txt — they go to My voice, not to your essays.
fr.voiceIntro: If you have texts you wrote yourself — posts, columns, drafts — put them on the My voice shelf. The assistant reads them to learn how you write, so its suggestions sound like you.
help.chat: Chat about the essay (with the selected text as its subject)
help.cite: Cite a source — the selected words, or a [n] at the caret
help.counters: Switch word counts · open goals & sprints
help.critique: Critique the section you’re in — the whole essay is in the Assistant menu
help.dashes: Become an em dash — and a true ellipsis …
help.dragSections: In the left panel, to reorder
help.edges: Left: sections & outline notes. Right: notes in the text (☉ pins).
help.email: Email a timestamped draft to yourself
help.esc: Closes whatever’s open; otherwise back to the shelf
help.find: Find & replace across the whole essay
help.later: Keep the selected passage for later
help.mark: Drop a “come back to this” mark
help.reorder: Reorder: the draft as cards — paragraphs, sentences, skeleton
help.rewrite: Versions of the selected text: write your own, ask the assistant, pick one
help.rightClick: Essays, shelf names, section headings, outline lines
help.title: Mutiny Shortcuts
help.undo: Undo big moves (section deletes, replace-all, passages kept for later) when not mid-typing
help.zoom: Zoom the page — text and column together ({reset} resets)
help.zoomControl: Bottom bar — +/− buttons, scroll it, or click the % to reset
hint.enter: Enter twice = a *** break · three times = new section · {help} shows everything else
import.done.one: {n} essay imported onto “{shelf}” — sections and breaks detected
import.done.other: {n} essays imported onto “{shelf}” — sections and breaks detected
import.noneInDrop: No .docx, .txt, or .md files in that drop
later.empty:
When a good paragraph is getting in the way of your argument, select it and drag it onto the Later tab below.
It leaves your draft but it is never lost.
later.needSelection: Select the passage first, then {key} keeps it for later
later.restoredEnd: Original spot is gone — restored to the end of {from}
later.saved: Kept for later — out of the way, never lost ({undo} to undo)
mark.needSection: Click into a section first, then {key} drops a mark
menu.aiRewrite: Versions of the Selected Text    Ctrl+Shift+M
nav.addTitle: Add a section at the end
nav.parasTitle: Show the first sentence of each paragraph
outline.deleteDesc: Removes the outline line and its gray ghost from the draft. Written prose is never touched.
outline.firstIsSection: The first line has to be a section
outline.hasWords: This section already has words in it — only empty section lines can become paragraphs
outline.hint: Enter — new line · Tab — turn an empty section line into a paragraph under the one above · Shift+Tab — turn a paragraph line into a section · Backspace on an empty line removes it
outline.paraPh: A sentence that will become a paragraph…
outline.sectionPh: The point of this section, in one sentence…
ro.buttonTitle: See the draft as cards and move paragraphs and sentences (Ctrl+Shift+O)
ro.cardsHint: Drag cards, or Alt+↑/↓ · double-click a card to move its sentences · Enter opens it in the draft
ro.oneSentence: This paragraph has a single sentence
ro.sentencesHint: Drag the sentences, or Alt+↑/↓ · Esc goes back
ro.skeletonHint: The first sentence of every paragraph: read on its own, it should tell your argument · click one to go there
search.replaced: {n} replaced across the whole essay — {undo} to undo
section.deleteDesc: Its words move to Later, recoverable anytime.
section.deleteEmptyDesc: Nothing to save — it just goes.
section.headTitle: Right-click for section options · click to add a title
section.removed: Section removed — its words are in Later, or {undo} to undo
shelf.authorChipTitle: Click to change your author name
shelf.deleteDesc: Essays move to another shelf. Nothing is deleted from disk.
shelf.exportCollectionDesc.one: Collect its essay, in shelf order, into a single document with a table of contents.
shelf.exportCollectionDesc.other: Collect its {n} essays, in shelf order, into a single document with a table of contents.
shelf.labelTitle: Click to rename · right-click to export or delete
shelf.onlyOne: This is your only shelf — add another before deleting this one
side.empty:
No notes yet.

Hit {key} while writing to drop a mark — a “come back to this” flag that never breaks your flow.
side.title: In the text
src.addPh: Paste a URL, a DOI or an ISBN…
src.blocked: That link points at this computer or your local network — Mutiny doesn’t fetch those
src.deleteCited.one: It is cited once in the text.
src.deleteCited.other: It is cited {n} times in the text.
src.deleteCitedDesc: Its citations go too: cited words stay as plain text, [n] marks are removed.
src.empty:
No sources yet.

Paste a link above — Mutiny fills in the title, author and date for you to check. Then cite it while you write with {key}.
src.fQuote: What it says, word for word (optional)
src.lookupFailed: Couldn’t read that page — check what’s filled in and complete the rest
src.needTitle: A source needs at least a title or a link
src.notFound: Nothing found for that — fill it in by hand
src.unrecognised: That doesn’t look like a URL, a DOI or an ISBN
stats.appearanceNone: No system theme found — using Mutiny’s
stats.appearanceNote: On Omarchy, the interface can follow the system theme. The page keeps its own look.
stats.sprintIdle: a small hill to charge up
stats.title: Goals & settings
stats.updates: Check for new versions when Mutiny opens
stats.updatesNote: Once a day, Mutiny reads the public list of releases on GitHub. Nothing about you or your essays is sent.
tab.darlingsTitle: Drag any selection here. It’s kept for later, not gone.
tile.coverDesc: Pick an image (2:3 works best). Or just drag one onto the essay.
tile.removeCoverDesc: Deletes the image from the essay folder. (To just hide it, use the ↻ on the essay.)
tile.removeDesc: Takes it off your shelves. The files stay safe in your Mutiny Library folder.
tile.removed: “{title}” removed from the shelves — its files are still in your Mutiny Library
tile.setGoalDesc: Adds a subtle progress bar to the cover.
tile.trashDesc: Sends the essay folder to your system trash, where you can recover it.
toast.hiccup: Something hiccuped — your words are safe, and the details were logged
tp.author: Author
tp.subtitle: Subtitle (optional)
tp.title: Untitled
tpl.conclusion: Conclusion — what changes if you are right?
tpl.conclusion.next: What the reader should do or think next
tpl.objection: The best objection — and your answer to it
tpl.objection.answer: Why it doesn’t change your conclusion
tpl.thesis: Your thesis — what are you claiming, in one sentence?
tpl.thesis.reader: What does the reader probably believe today?
typewriter.on: Typewriter scrolling ON — your line stays centered
update.failed: Couldn’t check for updates — try again later
voice.againMsg: Replace that copy with the essay as it is now?
voice.aiMsg: About {pct}% ({ai} of {total} words) is still exactly as the assistant proposed it. Used as reference, your style would partly learn from the AI and not only from you.
voice.aiStripDesc: Only the assistant's untouched text is left out. Your essay isn't changed.
voice.aiTitle: Part of this essay is the assistant's text, unchanged
voice.analysisTitle: What Mutiny sees in your texts
voice.blankMsg: estilo.md has text and this would erase it. Versions and the Chat would stop following a style.
voice.changedMsg: estilo.md was saved again after this window opened (a new version, or an edit outside Mutiny). Saving here replaces it with what this window shows.
voice.copyToDesc: A frozen copy, as reference for your style. The essay stays where it is.
voice.draftInfo: From {n} words in {texts} texts. Read it, fix what isn't you, then save.
voice.draftTitle: Your style, as the assistant sees it
voice.editedKeepDesc: The assistant starts from your file and keeps your rules unless your texts contradict them.
voice.editedMsg: Your style file has changes of your own.
voice.editedReplaceDesc: A new profile from your texts only. You'll see it before anything is saved.
voice.emptyEssay: That essay has no text yet
voice.emptyHint: Import .docx, .md or .txt files, or drag one of your essays here (it is copied, not moved).
voice.emptyTitle: Texts you wrote, so the assistant learns your voice
voice.expect.high: A solid profile. More text adds less from here on — variety of topics matters more than volume.
voice.expect.low: Enough for a sketch. Around 5,000 words from 3 or more texts, the assistant starts telling your habits from each text's topic.
voice.expect.medium: Good for a first profile: your connectors, rhythm, how you open and close. At 15,000+ words on varied topics it becomes solid.
voice.expect.veryLow: With under 2,000 words the assistant only catches the surface — tone, person, sentence length — and mistakes the topic for your style.
voice.fewMsg: With {n} words the profile will be basic: tone and rhythm, little of what makes you you. You can update it when you add more.
voice.genMsg: The assistant is reading {n} words from {texts} texts and writing estilo.md. You'll see it before anything is saved.
voice.genRunning: Your style is already being written
voice.grown: +{n} words since your style was generated
voice.handInfo: Written by hand. The assistant follows it as it is.
voice.m.perK: Small numbers are per 1,000 words. These counts are exact and made without AI; the assistant receives them when it writes your style.
voice.m.varHigh: you alternate short and long sentences a lot
voice.myStyleDesc: See or edit estilo.md, the profile the assistant follows.
voice.noneInfo: No style yet. Add texts to My voice and generate it, or write your own rules here.
voice.ready: ✦ Your style is ready — see it
voice.savedNew: Style saved — Versions and the Chat now follow it
voice.stylePlaceholder:
# My style

Short sentences. No “it is worth noting”. …
voice.tooLittle: At least {n} words are needed to generate a style
voice.useStyle: Use my style in Versions and the Chat
voice.warnOne: Only one text: the assistant can't tell your style from that text's topic. Add a couple more on other subjects.
voice.warnTopic: Your texts share a lot of vocabulary — they seem to be on similar topics. Texts on other subjects would help tell style from topic.
vs.keep: Keep the versions I don’t use in Later
vs.title: Versions
